contexts.text: (Such) are held by the Lord in thinking well... and are withheld from thinking evilly.
The Spirits hold his mind fixedly in the thought of some one thing. AC 5391:2.
The Angels... confess... that they are withheld from the evil and falsity of their proprium, and are held in good and truth, by the Lord...
The Angels... hold man in hope.
Is admitted no further than he can be kept in it.
That the Lord withheld them from evil, and held them in good. Signified.
By the good which He insinuates, the Lord withholds him... thus He holds man suspended between evil and good...
In childhood... man is held by the Lord in the affirmative...
It was necessary for them to be held... in the acknowledgement of Jehovah...
(In temptation) the Angels hold man in goods and truths...
In the other life they are held in evils, and thence in falsities. Explained.
(In temptations) the man is held by the Lord in goods and truths from within.
So long as the thought is held in the historicals... Then the thought can be held in the things which are signified...
For the Lord holds his mind in such things as are of charity and the derivative faith.
Not what he only... keeps in the memory.
Thus they hold others as it were in bonds.
Of the Lord's mercy, if man receives it, he is withheld from sin, and is held in good.
Therefore, the man is the rather held in incredulity...
In combats against falsities, man is held by the Lord in... that truth which he has persuaded himself to be truth...

They were withheld from openly committing evils (by) being held in external bonds... As with men (here), who, although inwardly devils, are yet held by these external bonds in the simulation of what is honest and just... and in order that they may be so held, Spirits who are in simple good are adjoined to them.
To be withheld from falsities (is signified), because... when a man is held by the Lord in good and truth, falsities and evils are removed...
But no one can be withheld from evil, and held in good, unless he has received this faculty by the exercise of charity (here).
The Lord does not take away evil, but He withholds man from it, and holds him in good. References.

Man is withheld by the Lord from evil, and is held in good; and he can be withheld from evil (there) in proportion as he has resisted evil (here); and he can then be held in good in proportion as (here) he has acted out good from affection. AC 9333:3.
God... from Himself, holds all things in their order.
Then first are evils remitted, for then the man is held by the Lord in goods and truths, and is withheld from evils. AC 9448.

They who are regenerate are continually held by the Lord in the good of faith and of love, and are then withheld from evils and falsities. Those who do not suffer themselves to be regenerated... are also withheld from evil, and are held in good... but the infernal loves... in which they are... turn the influx of good into evil...
The Lord keeps man in the freedom...

Evils... appear as if extirpated so far as man is held in good by the Lord; for when man is held in good he is withheld from evil; but no one can be withheld from evil and held in good but he who is in the good of faith and of charity...
All the Angels are withheld from their own proprium, and are held in the Lord's proprium... HH 595.

Man is withheld from sins when he is held in good by the Lord; and when he is held in good, it appears as if he were devoid of them... and man can be held in good in proportion as he is being reformed.
(Thus) unless man were held in freedom, good could not be provided for him.
That man is not let interiorly into truths... and goods... except in so far as he can be kept in them to the end of life. General article.
(In enchantments) they held the hearing and thus the mind of the other in their words...
He held it in his mouth that he would call them insane...
It is to be kept in mind...
He that holdeth the seven stars... () = that all Knowledges... are from Him.
Thou boldest My name () = the acknowledgement of the Divine in the Human...
Occurs. AE 514:4. AE 654:51.
